newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies close mostly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies close mostly higher in thin trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly higher in thin trade, as profit-taking ahead of Friday's U.S. September labor data pushed the U.S. dollar off its recent highs, traders and analysts said.
"The risk is the numbers come in soft and the dollar once again tests the highs," said Rob Fullem, a currency analyst at Natwest Markets.

Traders, on average, are looking for September nonfarm payrolls to rise 166,000, compared to August's increase of 250,000, and the unemployment rate is forecast to rise to 5.2 percent, from 5.1 percent in August.
"If wage pressures are under control, the dollar could go bid again," one futures floor source said.
Average hourly earnings for September are forecast to rise 0.2 percent, compared to up 0.5 percent in August.

However, any bullishness in the U.S. dollar-denominated markets are unlikely to take the December mark contract to $0.6488, which is roughly equivalent to the dollar/mark's year-and-a-half high of 1.5488 spot, in the near term. December marks' contract low is currently at $0.6537.
"The only objective for dollar/mark is really 1.55 at the lowest, but we haven't really come close," one trader said.
"It's going to be difficult to get up that way," Fullem said.
Fullem said higher crude oil prices provided light support to the currencies of net-exporting countries.
Although both sterling and Canadian dollar futures were lower, Fullem said a break-out to the upside in oil prices could take those currencies higher.
"If oil breaks to the upside, you may see sterling and Canadian dollars come back," he said.
The November crude oil contract on NYMEX rose near the $25.00-per-barrel level.
On technical factors alone, December Canadian dollars are expected to rise to $0.7390 and the $0.7400 level, traders said.
"Funds are extremely long Canadian dollars," another trader added.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000032 at $0.009061, marks were up $0.0007 at $0.6562, Swiss francs were up $0.0013 at $0.8026, sterling was unchanged at $1.5644, Canadian dollars were off $0.0004 at $0.7375, Australian dollars were $0.0046 lower at $0.7887 and Mexican pesos were down $0.000100 at $0.127200.
